description: Na₃FeO₃ is Aluminum carbonitride-like structured and crystallizes in the monoclinic Cc space group. There are six inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded to five O atoms to form distorted NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids that share corners with three FeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent NaO₄ trigonal pyramids, edges with two FeO₄ tetrahedra, and edges with two equivalent NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.32-2.66 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to four O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.32-2.43 Å. In the third Na site, Na is bonded to four O atoms to form distorted NaO₄ trigonal pyramids that share corners with four FeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent NaO₄ trigonal pyramids, and edges with two equivalent NaO₄ trigonal pyramids. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.21-2.39 Å. In the fourth Na site, Na is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to five O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.25-2.62 Å. In the fifth Na site, Na is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to four O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.30-2.44 Å. In the sixth Na site, Na is bonded to four O atoms to form distorted NaO₄ trigonal pyramids that share corners with three equivalent FeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids, corners with four NaO₄ trigonal pyramids, and  an edgeedge with one FeO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.27-2.40 Å. There are two inequivalent Fe sites. In the first Fe site, Fe is bonded to four O atoms to form FeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent FeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids, corners with two equivalent NaO₄ trigonal pyramids,  an edgeedge with one NaO₅ trigonal bipyramid, and  an edgeedge with one NaO₄ trigonal pyramid. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.84-1.94 Å. In the second Fe site, Fe is bonded to four O atoms to form FeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent FeO₄ tetrahedra,  a cornercorner with one NaO₅ trigonal bipyramid, corners with five NaO₄ trigonal pyramids, and  an edgeedge with one NaO₅ trigonal bipyramid. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.86-1.93 Å. There are six inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to three Na and two Fe atoms. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to three Na and two Fe atoms. In the third O site, O is bonded to five Na and one Fe atom to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing ONa₅Fe octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 47-55°. In the fourth O site, O is bonded to five Na and one Fe atom to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing ONa₅Fe octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 47-54°. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to five Na and one Fe atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to five Na and one Fe atom.
